The first thing we notice is that we can rewrite the terms of the series as powers of $\frac{1}{9}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{81}+⋯+\frac{1}{{9}^{n}}+⋯ & =1+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{{9}^{2}}+⋯+\frac{1}{{9}^{n}}+⋯ \\  & =1+\frac{1}{9}+{(\frac{1}{9})}^{2}+⋯+{(\frac{1}{9})}^{n}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\frac{1}{1-x}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1-x} & =1+x+{x}^{2}+{x}^{3}+⋯+{x}^{n}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{1}{9}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(1-\frac{1}{9})} & =1+\frac{1}{9}+{(\frac{1}{9})}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{9})}^{3}+⋯+{(\frac{1}{9})}^{n}+⋯ \\ \frac{9}{8} & =1+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{81}+\frac{1}{729}+⋯+\frac{1}{{9}^{n}}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\frac{9}{8}.$
